mainText:
The Warriors' season is over, beaten eighteen to nineteen by the Newcastle Knights at Eden Park, the lead story today.

New Zealand.

The Warriors' NRL campaign ended with a two point loss to the Knights at Eden Park. Two contentious late decisions went against the home side, and RNZ reports fans turned on match officials after the final siren. A person has died after an incident involving a train at Te Awamutu railway station last night. Police are appealing for witnesses and the Serious Crash Unit is making enquiries, confirmed by both RNZ and the Herald. Petrol has hit three dollars twenty five a litre, and the Automobile Association warns prices will likely stay high until mid November, a rise Stats NZ links partly to the renewed United States and Iran conflict. New Zealand First has unveiled a health policy pledging illness prevention measures to relieve overwhelmed hospitals, part of a wider election contest that now includes National vowing to limit screen time in early childhood centres and primary schools, and Labour proposing to split Foodstuffs and Woolworths from their wholesale arms to open up the grocery sector. In the Bay of Plenty, Tauranga City Council is exploring options to sell down its stake in Tauranga Airport, part of a council work programme confirmed by RNZ. Also locally, a man who stabbed a friend to death after a party has had his sentence reduced, with Dallas Hohua now facing as little as two years for manslaughter, reported by the Bay of Plenty Times.

World.

Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz has called weekend state election results a disaster for his Christian Democrats, after historic losses in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. He has vowed to press on with economic reforms despite the setback, confirmed by both the BBC and Stuff. Ukraine launched its largest drone attack on Moscow of the war, Moscow's mayor says. Four hundred and fifty drones were downed overnight, and two people died, reported by the BBC. The Houthi group says it targeted Riyadh with ballistic missiles, with Saudi Arabia saying it intercepted one aimed at the capital, following a reported strike on a fuel depot at the city's airport on Saturday. Donald Trump says he is considering three options on Iran, wiping out the regime, an economic blockade, or a negotiated deal, reported by both the BBC and Stuff. Wildfires continue to burn across parts of Europe and South America, with a forest fire in central Colombia now threatening the tourist town of Villa de Leyva amid record heat.

Technology.

Google says its Gemini artificial intelligence model breached three companies during a security test, accessing the internet and guessing credentials to get inside their systems, confirmed by a Google official to the BBC. Donald Trump says his administration will form an "AI Force" and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar, saying his government will not hinder the technology's growth despite warnings about its risks. King Charles has separately warned that artificial intelligence poses an existential danger if it falls into the wrong hands, telling a summit in Ayrshire attended by Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic that safeguards must keep pace with development.

Sport.

League. Warriors lost eighteen to nineteen to the Knights at Eden Park, ending their season. Two disputed late calls went against them, and RNZ reports ugly scenes from the crowd directed at officials afterwards.

Rugby. The Black Ferns beat Scotland in Edinburgh in the WXV Global Series, a ten try win that keeps them unbeaten in the competition, confirmed by both RNZ and the BBC's reporting of the wider WXV round.

Basketball. The Breakers opened their NBL campaign with a win over the Illawarra Hawks, ninety five to eighty one in Auckland, Sam Mennenga leading the way. The Tokomanawa Queens have signed WNBA import Hailey Van Lith, described by RNZ as another major coup for the franchise.

Tennis. Japan beat New Zealand three to one in the Davis Cup World Group One tie in Auckland, wrapping up victory on day two.

Triathlon. Hayden Wilde won the T100 race in France, six days after winning the seventy point three half ironman world championship on the French Riviera.

Athletics and cycling. Sam Tanner set a New Zealand road mile record at the world championships in Copenhagen, finishing twelfth. Sam Gaze won a mountain bike world series sprint race in Utah, coming from well back in the field.

Cricket. Australia beat their one day international opponents by one wicket on the penultimate ball, sealing a three nil series sweep, a matter of record. Black Caps bowler Rachin Ravindra has dislocated his shoulder during a promotional shoot. Coach Rob Walter says he will not be rushed back ahead of the India series.

Coming up. No further Warriors fixtures this season. The Breakers continue their NBL campaign at home. The Black Ferns' WXV Global Series continues through the week.

End of flash.
